label: Cat fur color
summary: The fur color of the cat that the character owns in a cat story: brown, gray, orange, black or white.
details: Works on a character. It looks at the character's own cat story (`story_cycle_pet_cat`) and reads its stored fur color. Vanilla's text for white is not shown in the input.

label: Cat fur color (any scope)
summary: The same fur colors, read from the variable `cat_fur_color` of whatever the text is run on (for example a story).
details: Works on any kind of scope, not only a character. Vanilla's cat description line uses it on a story.

label: Cat or dog name
summary: The name of a pet from a cat or dog story: a custom name, or one of the fixed dog and cat names.
details: Works on a character. The entry is chosen from flags in character variables such as `story_cycle_dog_name`, `book_topic_dog_name` and `sacrificed_dog_name`. The first entry (dog_name, used when the flag is `custom`) shows the text stored under `story_cycle_dog_name`. Fixed dog names include Amiable, Nosewise and Holdfast, followed by cat names. 11 more entries exist than shown.

label: Cat or dog name (any scope)
summary: The same pet names as the character version, for any kind of scope.
details: Same entries: a custom dog name plus fixed dog and cat names such as Amiable, Nosewise and Holdfast. Its triggers read the same name variables on the scope it runs on.

label: Cat sex word
summary: The cat's sex as a word: "female" or "male".
details: Works on a character. It uses the cat story the character owns (`story_cycle_pet_cat`) and its `cat_gender` flag.

label: Cat sex word (any scope)
summary: The words "female" or "male", read from the `cat_gender` variable of the scope it runs on.
details: Works on any kind of scope.

label: Cat girl or boy
summary: The cat as "girl" or "boy".
details: Works on a character, from the `cat_gender` flag of the cat story the character owns.

label: Cat girl or boy (any scope)
summary: The words "girl" or "boy", read from the `cat_gender` variable of the scope it runs on.
details: Works on any kind of scope.

label: Cat her or him
summary: The cat as an object pronoun: "her" or "him".
details: Works on a character, from the `cat_gender` flag of the cat story the character owns.

label: Cat her or him (any scope)
summary: The words "her" or "him", read from the `cat_gender` variable of the scope it runs on.
details: Works on any kind of scope.

label: Cat her or his
summary: The cat as a possessive: "her" or "his".
details: Works on a character, from the `cat_gender` flag of the cat story the character owns.

label: Cat her or his (any scope)
summary: The words "her" or "his", read from the `cat_gender` variable of the scope it runs on.
details: Works on any kind of scope.

label: Cat herself or himself
summary: The cat as a reflexive pronoun: "herself" or "himself".
details: Works on a character, from the `cat_gender` flag of the cat story the character owns.

label: Cat herself or himself (any scope)
summary: The words "herself" or "himself", read from the `cat_gender` variable of the scope it runs on.
details: Works on any kind of scope.

label: Cat age text
summary: The cat's age: "a kitten" under 1, otherwise "N years old".
details: Works on any kind of scope. It reads the variable `cat_age_variable`: below 1 gives the kitten text, 1 or more gives the number (written without decimals) plus "years old".

label: Cat name
summary: The cat's name: a custom name, or one of the fixed names (Gyb, Mite, Gray, Flame, Snow, Shadow, Paws, Mittens, Hunter and more).
details: Works on a character. The entry is chosen from flags in the character's variables (`story_cycle_cat_name`, `book_topic_cat_name`, `sacrificed_cat_name`). The first entry (cat_name, flag `custom`) shows the text stored under `story_cycle_cat_name`. The list also has name_lil_city, name_pride_of_city, name_tail_of_city and name_tigon; 7 entries are not shown here.

label: Cat name (any scope)
summary: The cat's name for any kind of scope: "not yet chosen" while no name is set, otherwise a custom or fixed name.
details: The first entry (not_yet_chosen) applies when the scope has no `story_cycle_cat_name` variable. The custom name is read from the story's owner. 8 entries are not shown here.

label: Cat name possessive
summary: The cat's name as a possessive: "Mittens'", "Paws'", or the name plus 's for any other name.
details: Works on a character. Mittens and Paws (checked on `story_cycle_cat_name`) get their own entries without the extra s; the last entry has no condition and builds the name from CatStoryName plus 's.

label: Cat name possessive (any scope)
summary: The cat's name as a possessive, for any kind of scope.
details: Same entries as the character version: "Mittens'", "Paws'" and the general name plus 's.

label: Cat she or he
summary: The cat as a subject pronoun: "she" or "he".
details: Works on a character, from the `cat_gender` flag of the cat story the character owns.

label: Cat she or he (any scope)
summary: The words "she" or "he", read from the `cat_gender` variable of the scope it runs on.
details: Works on any kind of scope.

label: Orange cat description
summary: A line about an orange male cat being dumb but very sweet, or an empty text for every other cat.
details: Works on any kind of scope. The line appears only when `cat_fur_color` is orange and `cat_gender` is male; otherwise the empty blank_line entry is used. The line starts with a line break and is built from the cat's pronoun, fur color and girl/boy texts, reading like "He is a dumb orange boy, but very sweet."

label: Tributary request
summary: What a tributary asks for, as a phrase: trade access, a future marriage, a say at the palace, or relief from duties.
details: Works on a character. The phrase follows the saved scope `ask` (flag trade, marriage or politics); with any other value or none, the generic request (relief from obligations) is used. The wording reads as a petition to an emperor.

label: Funeral ceremony description
summary: A short description of a funeral ceremony, such as public bewailment, sky burial, ground burial, cremation or mummification.
details: Works on a character. Which one is used depends on faith: a West African pagan faith that qualifies for feudalisation gets the bewailment, a faith with the sky burial rite gets sky burial, an Abrahamic faith gets ground burial, the Germanic religion gets cremation, the mummification rite gets mummification; anything else gets a general ceremony text. Each text is a sentence or two about how the body is treated.

label: Funeral ceremony name
summary: The name of a funeral ceremony, such as Public Bewailment, Sky Burial, Burial or Cremation.
details: Works on a character. It is chosen by the same faith and rite conditions as CeremonyDesc, which gives the matching description; the last entry is a general ceremony name.

label: Difficulty label
summary: A colored difficulty word for a character: Impossible, Extremely Hard, Very Hard, Hard, or a normal one.
details: Works on a character. It goes by `character_difficulty_value`: 500 or more is Impossible, 300 to 499 Extremely Hard, 150 to 299 Very Hard, 50 to 149 Hard, and below 50 uses the normal entry (its text is not shown in the input). The words use the text styles `difficulty_very_hard`, `difficulty_hard` and `difficulty_medium`.

label: Power sharing category name
summary: The heading for the power sharing group in the interaction menu: a diarch's title, or "Power Sharing".
details: Works on a character. The diarch title (the player's diarch title) is used when the saved scope `second` is a diarch whose liege is the character; in every other case the fallback "Power Sharing" is shown.

label: Vassal category name
summary: The heading for the vassal-relations group in the interaction menu, naming what the other character is to the character: Liege, Suzerain, governor, Vassal, tributary, fellow governor, fellow vassal, courtier, or a fallback.
details: Works on a character, with the saved scope `second` as the other one. The first entry whose condition holds is used, for example Liege when the character is a vassal or lower vassal of `second`, Suzerain when the character is a tributary of `second`, Courtier when `second` is a courtier of the character. Liege, Suzerain and Vassal are plain words; the governor entry uses the game's governor term. The texts of the later entries are not shown in the input.

label: Character introduction
summary: A way to introduce a character in a text: by name when they hold a title, otherwise as "a nobleman/noblewoman/commoner from ...".
details: Works on a character. Entries are tried in this order: the character has a primary title (name); the liege has a primary title ("from" the liege's primary title); the character is somewhere with a barony ("from" the current location); otherwise just the name and "a nobleman/noblewoman/commoner". Low-born characters are named by first name only, nobles by full name. Despite "NoComma" in the key, the shown entries contain a comma before "a ...". The texts of the location and plain entries are not shown in the input.

label: Child word by sex
summary: A word for the character's children: daughter, son, daughters, sons, or children.
details: Works on a character. The plural entries check the children: all girls gives daughters, all boys gives sons, a mix gives children. The two singular entries (daughter, son) test `any_sibling = { always = no }` inside the child check, which cannot be true as written, so they appear never to be chosen.

label: Pet name for a child
summary: A playful pet name for a child: imp, rapscallion, rascal or scamp.
details: Works on a character. Its four entries have no conditions, and the file marks it `random_valid = yes`.

label: Childhood personality trait
summary: The name of the character's childhood personality trait: charming, rowdy, bossy, curious or pensive.
details: Works on a character. The entry is chosen by which of these traits the character has; each shows the trait's own name as written for that character.

label: Childhood trait activity
summary: A short phrase for something a child likes to do, such as "make a new friend" (charming) or "learn something new" (curious).
details: Works on a character. Curious, pensive and rowdy entries check their own trait. Vanilla's bossy entry ("train a new minion") checks for the charming trait, the same as the charming entry (the fallback), so bossy children are not matched by it. The file marks it `random_valid = yes`.

label: Christian relic description
summary: A phrase naming a Christian relic, such as a nail from the cross, a thorn from the crown, Jesus' sandals or the girdle of Mary.
details: Works on a character. The relic comes from the saved scope `christian_relic_name` (flags nail, thorn, sandals, girdle, skull, arm and so on). The ten entries also cover a loincloth, the cross, the Crown of Thorns and the Veil of Veronica. The file marks it `random_valid = yes`.

label: Christian relic name
summary: The short name of a Christian relic, such as Holy Nail, Holy Thorn or Sandals of Jesus.
details: Works on a character. It uses the same saved scope `christian_relic_name` as ChristianRelic. For girdle, skull, arm and loincloth it uses the same text keys as the description list, so those show the longer phrase.

label: Mythical founder name
summary: The name of a legendary founder, such as Charles the Hammer, Alexander the Great, Lech, Czech, Rus, Arthur or Romulus, with a fallback.
details: Works on a character. The founder comes from the character's variable `mythical_founder` (a flag). The file marks it `random_valid = yes`. 2 entries are not shown here; the list ends with a fallback. Used for claiming a throne, going by the key name.

label: Founder herself, himself, themselves
summary: The word himself, herself or themselves, matching the mythical founder.
details: Works on a character. It reads `mythical_founder`: himself for founders such as Charles, Alexander, Arthur and Romulus, herself for Zenobia, themselves for groups such as the pharaohs.

label: Family relation word
summary: The word for what the other character (saved scope `second`) is to this character: mother, father, grandparent, child, grandchild, sibling, niece or nephew, aunt or uncle, hostage, warden, cousin.
details: Works on a character. The entries test `second` against the character, for example mother is chosen when `second` is female and has the character as a child. Male and female forms are separate entries. 6 entries are not shown here.

label: Taught commander trait
summary: The name of the commander trait a character is being taught, such as Logistician, Military Engineer, Aggressive Attacker or Unyielding Defender.
details: Works on a character. The trait is read from the variable `commander_trait_being_taught` (a flag). Each entry shows the trait's name with its hover text. The list also holds skill-style entries (open terrain expert, forest fighter, organizer and similar). 5 entries are not shown here.

label: Taught commander trait (plain)
summary: The plain name of the commander trait being taught, such as Logistician or Military Engineer, with no hover text.
details: Works on a character. It reads the same `commander_trait_being_taught` variable as CommanderTraitBeingTaught. The shown text for unyielding defender is just "Defender". 5 entries are not shown here.

label: Commander skill phrase
summary: A short phrase for the skill a commander trait stands for, such as "supply", "siege-craft", "vicious charges and fierce attacks" or "sound defense".
details: Works on a character. It reads the same `commander_trait_being_taught` variable, with one entry per trait. 5 entries are not shown here.

label: Epic composer reference
summary: How the creator of a commissioned epic is named: the composer by titled first name, or "my" plus bards or scribes.
details: Works on a character. If the saved scope `second` exists, it is the composer and is named by titled first name; otherwise the text says "my" plus CommissionEpicScribes.

label: Epic composer has or have
summary: The verb "has" for one composer, or "have" for several scribes.
details: Works on a character. "has" is used when the saved scope `second` exists, otherwise "have". It keeps the sentence grammatical with CommissionEpicComposer.

label: Epic composer their
summary: The possessive for the epic's creator: his or her for the composer (by their sex), "their" for scribes.
details: Works on a character. The composer form is used when the saved scope `second` exists.

label: Epic composer them
summary: The object pronoun for the epic's creator: him or her for the composer, "them" for scribes.
details: Works on a character. The composer form is used when the saved scope `second` exists.

label: Epic composer they
summary: The subject pronoun for the epic's creator: he or she for the composer, "they" for scribes.
details: Works on a character. The composer form is used when the saved scope `second` exists.

label: Epic scribe word
summary: The word for one epic writer: "bard" or "scribe".
details: Works on a character. "bard" is used when the character's government is tribal (`government_is_tribal`), otherwise "scribe".

label: Epic scribes word
summary: The plural word for epic writers: "bards" or "scribes".
details: Works on a character. "bards" is used when the character's government is tribal, otherwise "scribes".

label: Compliment adjective
summary: A flattering adjective for a character, such as handsome, fair, impressive, benevolent, charming, valiant or eloquent, with a fallback.
details: Works on a character. Each word is tied to a condition: for example handsome (men) and fair (women) need the good-looks trait, benign and similar words depend on the character's compassion. Many words have a separate female entry that shows the same text in the examples. The file marks it `random_valid = yes`. 58 entries are not shown here.

label: Compliment adjective with article
summary: The same flattering adjectives with "a" or "an" in front, such as "a fair" or "an impressive".
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as ComplimentAdjective. The article matches the adjective. The file marks it `random_valid = yes`. 58 entries are not shown here.

label: Compliment adjective, "the most" genitive
summary: A "the most ..." form of the flattering adjectives in the genitive case, defined in the game's Polish custom localization.
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as ComplimentAdjective. The input shows no texts. The genitive case and "the most" come from the key name; the file is the Polish one (00_pl_custom_loc.txt), so the form matters for Polish text. The file marks it `random_valid = yes`.

label: Compliment sentence
summary: A whole flattering sentence, such as "were beauty a crown, you would outrank kings" or "wit such as yours is rarer than frankincense".
details: Works on a character. Each sentence has its own condition, for example the beauty one needs good looks and adulthood, the wit one needs a smart trait or a high learning or diplomacy skill, the first one a good relationship with the speaker or enough opinion of them. The file marks it `random_valid = yes`. 3 entries are not shown here; the list ends with a fallback.

label: Composition detail
summary: A story detail for a composed work: loyal horse, raging ox, scheming witch, magical sword, dragon, emperor, river, mountain or hermit.
details: Works on a character. It reads the variable `composition_detail` (a flag). Only the first four texts are shown in the input.

label: Composition type
summary: The kind of work: song, chronicle or poem.
details: Works on a character. It reads the variable `composition_type` (a flag).

label: Composition action (ongoing)
summary: What one does with the work, in the ongoing form: "listening to" a song, "reading" a chronicle or poem.
details: Works on a character. It reads `composition_type`.

label: Composition action (past)
summary: What one did with the work, in the past form: "listened to" a song, "read" a chronicle or poem.
details: Works on a character. It reads `composition_type`.

label: Composition type (any scope)
summary: The kind of work (song, chronicle or poem), for any kind of scope.
details: Reads `composition_type` on the scope it runs on.

label: Glorious composition type (accusative)
summary: The kind of work (song, chronicle or poem) in a "glorious" accusative form, defined in the game's Polish custom localization.
details: Works on a character, reading `composition_type`. The input shows no texts, so the exact words are unknown; "glorious" and "accusative" come from the key names, and the file is the Polish one (00_pl_custom_loc.txt).

label: Concubine by sex
summary: The game concept link for a concubine: the female one for a woman, the male one for a man.
details: Works on a character, chosen by whether the character is female. The texts are links to the game's concept pages for female and male concubines.

label: Board game type
summary: The name of a board game in a contest: pachisi, hnefatafl, tabula, go, fidchell or chess.
details: Works on an activity, not on a character. The game depends on the region of the activity's location (each of the first five has its own region trigger); chess is the fallback.

label: Race horse sex
summary: The word for the horse's sex in a horse race: mare or stallion.
details: Works on a character. Mare is used when the variable `contest_horse_race_gender` is female; otherwise stallion.

label: Race horse her or him
summary: The object pronoun for a race horse: "her" or "him".
details: Works on a character. "her" when `contest_horse_race_gender` is female, otherwise "him".

label: Race horse her or his
summary: The possessive for a race horse: "her" or "his".
details: Works on a character. "her" when `contest_horse_race_gender` is female, otherwise "his".

label: Race horse name
summary: A name for a race horse or war horse: from legend (Sleipnir, Bucephalus, Pegasus, Rocinante), from colors and weather, from the owner's faith, culture or capital, or jokes (Sir Horsington).
details: Works on a character. The entry is chosen by the variable `contest_horse_race_name` (a flag). Names with the owner's faith use that faith's god names in the possessive, for example "... Child" or "... Gambit". 247 more entries are listed than shown. Oddities: some keys appear more than once (racehorse_name_winner three times, racehorse_name_chestnut twice), and racehorse_name_faith_knowledge_god uses the night god's name, which looks like a copy mistake.

label: Race horse name ending
summary: A second word for a race horse's name, a body part or motion: bolt, bound, blaze, coat, dart, dash, face, feet, hoof, mane, socks, star, tail and more.
details: Works on a character. The entry is chosen by the variable `contest_horse_race_name_2` (a flag), a second name part next to ContestHorseRaceName. 17 entries are not shown here. The key racehorse_name_2_socks is listed twice.

label: Race horse she or he
summary: The subject pronoun for a race horse: "she" or "he".
details: Works on a character. "she" when `contest_horse_race_gender` is female, otherwise "he".

label: Race track word
summary: The word for the race ground: "maydan" or "track".
details: Works on an activity, not on a character. "maydan" when the variable `contest_horse_race_variant` is maydan; otherwise "track".

label: Opinion of me line
summary: A tooltip line giving the character's opinion of the player, with its sign, such as "opinion of me: +10".
details: Works on a character. It has one entry, used only when the character is not the local player. The number is shown with a plus or minus sign.

label: Spouse tooltip line
summary: A tooltip line about the character's partner: spouse, betrothed, concubine of someone, or "Unmarried".
details: Works on a character. It is checked in that order: married, betrothed, concubine, else unmarried. The first two show the name of the primary spouse or betrothed; the concubine line shows the name of the one they are a concubine of.

label: Coronation artifact needed
summary: The text for what a coronation needs: Crown, Regalia, or Crown or Regalia.
details: Works on a faith, not on a character. The faith's own checks (a proper crown artifact, a proper regalia artifact) decide; if neither alone applies, the fallback says Crown or Regalia.

label: Council position name
summary: The title of the character's council position, such as Grand Chancellor, Minister of War, Minister of Revenue or Imperial Censor, with ordinary councillor titles for other cases.
details: Works on a character. The celestial government's imperial titles need both the minister title and the matching council position (for example the minister of war title with the marshal position). Other entries go by council position alone (minister of personnel, justice, works, grand marshal and the ordinary councillor positions; their texts are not shown). 3 entries are not shown here.

label: Council position name (PL)
summary: The name of the character's council position (Chancellor, Spouse, Marshal, Steward and so on), with a fallback, from the game's Polish relations file.
details: Works on a character. Each entry checks `has_council_position` for one position. It is defined in 00_pl_relations.txt, so PL most likely means Polish; the shown texts are plain singular names.

label: Creator god name (CEL form)
summary: The name of a faith's creator or high god in a special form, one entry per religion (Christianity, Buddhism and many more).
details: Works on a faith. Each entry checks the faith's religion tag (or one specific faith). It is defined in the game's Polish extra file (00_pl_custom_loc_extra.txt); the input shows no texts, so what the CEL form is cannot be confirmed. 32 entries are not shown here.

label: Criminal adjective
summary: An insulting adjective for a criminal: horrendous, villainous, terrible, loathsome, vile, heinous, murderous, conniving, violent or barbaric.
details: Works on a character. The first six have no condition; murderous, conniving and the later ones need the gallowsbait trait with enough experience on a matching track (for example 50 or more on the marauder track for murderous). The file marks it `random_valid = yes`.

label: Crier insult
summary: A mocking physical description a town crier uses for a criminal: big-nosed, snub-nosed, weak-chinned, small-headed, buck-toothed, three-fingered or cross-eyed.
details: Works on a character. The entries have no conditions, and the file marks it `random_valid = yes`.

label: Cultural curse
summary: A swear word or oath tied to a faith or culture, such as "by the blood", "helvete", "merde" or "shit".
details: Works on a character. The first three entries need a Christian faith; others depend on the character's culture name list (for example Norwegian or Swedish for helvete). Some use the faith's high god name in the possessive, for example "[God's] wounds". The file marks it `random_valid = yes`. 51 entries are not shown here.

label: Signature weapon (DE 10)
summary: The name of the character's signature weapon: sword, mace, axe, hammer, spear or dagger.
details: Works on a character. The weapon comes from the variable `signature_weapon` (a flag); sword is the fallback. One of four near-identical lists (DE_10 to DE_13), part of the game's German (DE) custom localization. The input shows no texts.

label: Signature weapon (DE 11)
summary: The name of the character's signature weapon: sword, mace, axe, hammer, spear or dagger.
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as DE_10_signature_weapon (the variable `signature_weapon`, sword as fallback). The input shows no texts.

label: Signature weapon (DE 12)
summary: The name of the character's signature weapon: sword, mace, axe, hammer, spear or dagger.
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as DE_10_signature_weapon (the variable `signature_weapon`, sword as fallback). The input shows no texts.

label: Signature weapon (DE 13)
summary: The name of the character's signature weapon: sword, mace, axe, hammer, spear or dagger.
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as DE_10_signature_weapon (the variable `signature_weapon`, sword as fallback). The input shows no texts.

label: Arm or arms
summary: The word "arm" for a maimed character, "arms" for anyone else.
details: Works on a character. Part of the game's German (DE) custom localization, which varies a word by the character's condition. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Eye or eyes
summary: The word "eye" for a one-eyed character, "eyes" for anyone else.
details: Works on a character. Part of the game's German (DE) custom localization. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Fitting god name
summary: A way to name the divine in a motto: "God", "the perfected ones", "the divine" or "the gods", by the faith of the house head.
details: Works on a character. It looks at the faith of the house's last house head: Christian, Islamic or Jewish gives "God", Buddhist the perfected ones, dualist or Zoroastrian the divine, every other religion the gods. The custom_loc_god entry has a condition that is never true (`always = no`) and is the fallback. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Grit type
summary: What the grit is made of, by the terrain at the character's location: grit, dirt, sand, bog water, twigs, wet leaves or dry grass.
details: Works on a character. For example mountains (the fallback) give grit, plains, farmlands, hills or floodplains dirt, deserts and oases sand, wetlands bog water, forest or taiga twigs. Part of the game's German (DE) single-combat texts. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Ground type
summary: What the ground is like, by the terrain at the character's location: dust, dirt, rocks, sandy rocks, sand, wet grass, mulch or grass.
details: Works on a character. When the saved scope `locale` exists, dust is the fallback; otherwise terrain decides, for example farmlands, hills or drylands give dirt, mountains rocks, desert mountains sandy rocks, deserts and oases sand. Part of the game's German (DE) single-combat texts. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Hand or hands
summary: The word "hand" for a maimed character, "hands" for anyone else.
details: Works on a character. Part of the game's German (DE) custom localization. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Mask or face
summary: The word "mask" for a disfigured character, "face" for anyone else.
details: Works on a character. Part of the game's German (DE) custom localization. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Signature weapon action
summary: What a character does with their signature weapon: draws the sword, lifts the mace, hefts the axe, raises the hammer, couches the spear or brandishes the dagger.
details: Works on a character. The weapon comes from the variable `signature_weapon` (a flag); sword is the fallback. The input shows no texts; the verbs come from the entry keys.

label: Heavy weapon blow attempted
summary: The kind of heavy blow tried with the signature weapon: slash, crush or pierce.
details: Works on a character. Sword, axe and dagger give slash (the fallback), mace and hammer crush, spear pierce, by the variable `signature_weapon`. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Heavy weapon blows attempted (plural)
summary: The plural form of the heavy blow tried with the signature weapon: slash, crush or pierce.
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as DE_1_SignatureWeaponAttemptedHeavy. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Light weapon blow attempted
summary: The kind of light blow tried with the signature weapon: slash, crush or pierce.
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as DE_1_SignatureWeaponAttemptedHeavy. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Light weapon blows attempted (plural)
summary: The plural form of the light blow tried with the signature weapon: slash, crush or pierce.
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as DE_1_SignatureWeaponAttemptedHeavy. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Weapon breaks (past)
summary: How the signature weapon gives way: bend the blade (sword, dagger), snap the haft (spear, axe) or bend the haft (hammer, mace).
details: Works on a character, by the variable `signature_weapon`. The entry keys are in the base form ("bend", "snap"), while the next list (PastTense2) has "bent", "snapped"; what the shown texts give is not in the input, so the tense is not confirmed.

label: Weapon breaks (past, second form)
summary: How the signature weapon gave way: bent the blade (sword, dagger), snapped the haft (spear, axe) or bent the haft (hammer, mace).
details: Works on a character, by the variable `signature_weapon`. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Weapon breaks (-ing form)
summary: How the signature weapon is giving way: bending the blade (sword, dagger), snapping the haft (spear, axe) or bending the haft (hammer, mace).
details: Works on a character, by the variable `signature_weapon`. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Critical weapon blow
summary: The kind of critical blow dealt with the signature weapon: slash, crush or pierce.
details: Works on a character. Sword, axe and dagger give slash (the fallback), mace and hammer crush, spear pierce, by the variable `signature_weapon`. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Critical weapon blow (present)
summary: The present-tense form of the critical blow with the signature weapon: slash, crush or pierce.
details: Works on a character, with the same conditions as DE_1_SignatureWeaponCritical. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Weapon end material
summary: What the end of the signature weapon is made of: wood for a spear or axe, metal for the others.
details: Works on a character, by the variable `signature_weapon`; metal is the fallback. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Weapon flourish
summary: How the signature weapon is flourished: whirling (sword, axe), flailing (mace, hammer, dagger) or swinging (spear).
details: Works on a character, by the variable `signature_weapon`; whirling is the fallback. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.

label: Weapon kill type
summary: How the signature weapon kills: crush (mace, hammer), run through (sword, spear), cut down (axe) or gut (dagger).
details: Works on a character, by the variable `signature_weapon`; cut down is the fallback. The input shows no texts; the words come from the entry keys.
